triage.note: The mutation half of ui-font-link-nonblocking, in the S5 `-regression` shape (expect.min_failures == max_failures pins an EXACT count, so a regressed miss and a regressed over-fire both go red). The fixture carries nine links and exactly four must fire: (3) a second external sheet with the media/onload attributes removed — the 'attribute removed' and 'second blocking link' mutations are the same tag; (4) a `media=print` sheet with no onload, which never applies on screen; (7) the same blocking link written with UNQUOTED attribute values (PR #33 R1 — valid HTML that the quoted-only ATTR_RE never saw, so the tag was skipped as 'not a stylesheet'); (9) a SECOND unquoted blocking link (PR #33 R5, added by L1 2026-08-23 — with only one unquoted link the round-0 parser's miss of (7) and its over-fire on (8) cancelled to the same count of 3, so the committed pin could not go red on a revert of the round-1 repair as a whole; two unquoted links make the pin 4 here and 3 at the round-0 parser). The five that must NOT fire are the shipped fix itself, its `<noscript>` fallback, a same-origin sheet, an HTML-commented-out link, and (8) a `media="not all"` sheet promoted by `this.media='ALL'` (PR #33 R2 — `not all` is the other standard non-blocking idiom and media values are case-insensitive; both were false positives before round 1). A check that pinned the literal attribute string instead of the property would count (1) green by accident and (4) green by mistake; this fixture is what says it does neither.
